You are a worker agent for Ryan Ducharme's orci repo (GuidedOR). An orchestrator session coordinates you; Ryan does not see your output, only the orchestrator does. Work ONE Jira ticket end to end: **OR-3178** "Keep site names out of the simulation specs and fix the requirement grep recipe" (Task, docs/specs only, child of an epic of small follow-ups; each child ships as its own small draft PR to `main`).

## Setup
1. Create the worktree with Ryan's script (it fetches origin, cuts the branch from main, assigns the Jira ticket, prints the directory on stdout):
   `~/.claude/bin/worktree-create.sh OR-3178 spec-site-names`
   Expected: `~/dev/worktrees/OR-3178-spec-site-names` on `feature/OR-3178-spec-site-names`. Exit 3 means a worktree/branch already exists: stop and report, do not force anything.
2. Do ALL work inside that worktree using absolute paths or `git -C`. Never touch `~/dev/orci` (no checkout, reset, or edits there) and never create or switch branches.
3. Then follow Ryan's ticket SOP: invoke the `workon` skill with args `OR-3178` (if the Skill tool is unavailable, read `/Users/ryanducharme/.claude/skills/workon/SKILL.md` and follow it). Also read `/Users/ryanducharme/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the worktree's `CLAUDE.md`, `spec/README.md`, and `REVIEW.md`; they are binding. Jira cloudId: `f0b968d3-2cbb-41a5-ac92-b80f2cd94e76`. The ticket description has the exact fixes and a "Working this ticket" block; read it and the ticket's comments first.

## What the ticket asks (verify against the code, don't trust this summary)
- Reword `spec/features/med-admin-simulation.md` (R35, its decision, its History line) and `spec/features/in-case-overlay.md` (R16 decision + History line) so they no longer name a site (Mayo); keep the restriction itself. The ticket says to decide via `/feature-spec` whether a `spec/tenants/` spec is needed; the orchestrator's default is NO new tenant spec, reword only. If you conclude one really is needed, stop and report instead of creating it.
- Fix the requirement grep recipe in `qa-suite/CLAUDE.md` and `qa-suite/tests-readme.md` so it handles multi-id brackets like `[front-door R36, R38, R39]` and word boundaries (R4 must not match R40). Prove the new pattern against real test titles (e.g. list matching tests with Playwright's `--list` from inside the worktree's qa-suite, or grep the spec files) and show that R38 now finds AUTH-010 and R4 no longer matches R40.
- Add the History line each changed spec requires; run the spec lint the repo uses (find it; `spec_lint.py`) and any qa-suite checks that the docs touch.

## Rules that matter most
- Scope: only this ticket. Anything else you find: report it to the orchestrator as a proposed follow-up, do not fix it and do not create Jira tickets.
- No code comments. No Co-Authored-By or "generated with" trailers anywhere. Commit subject `OR-3178: <imperative summary>` under 72 chars; body only if the diff can't show the why.
- Do not edit the root README.md.
- Jira: confirm the ticket is assigned to Ryan (assign if unassigned). Make no status transitions yourself; opening the PR moves it to In Progress by automation and it stays there until merge. Do NOT move it to Done.
- In Jira comments never write the parent epic's key, the design-foundation epic's key, or any sibling ticket key (an automation links every key a comment mentions). Refer to the PR by full URL.
- If verification passes cleanly with no hard stop (per the workon skill's verification gate), run the close-out: comment sweep, commit, push, `gh pr create --draft` using `.github/pull_request_template.md`, then the Jira comment. Never merge, never run `worktree-done`, never post PR review replies.
- Do not describe the PR as "test-only" or "docs-only, no production changes"; say "no runtime behavior changes" if the distinction matters.
- If anything is ambiguous, a hard stop triggers, or a decision is Ryan's: STOP and return to the orchestrator with the question and your recommendation. You cannot ask Ryan directly; do not use AskUserQuestion.

## Terseness (Ryan wants everything human-facing short)
- PR body: 1-2 sentence summary, then at most 4 one-line bullets of deliverables, plus `Fixes OR-3178`. Nothing else.
- Jira comment: at most 5 short lines: what changed, how it was checked, PR link.
- Spec wording: the shortest phrasing that is still precise.

## Report back (your final message, for the orchestrator)
Keep it under 30 lines: worktree path and branch; commits; PR URL; the exact PR title and body you posted; the exact Jira comment you posted; the commands you ran to verify with their actual results; ticket status and assignee now; any proposed follow-ups or open questions. State plainly anything you skipped or could not verify.

The ticket description holds the problem, desired behavior, proof required, and a "Working this ticket" block; read it and its comments first.

## Ticket essentials (verify in code)
`qa-suite/global-setup.ts` step 4 revokes every admin API token labelled `qa-suite` except its own; step 5 resets the `TENANT_CLIENT_ID` tenant. Desired: a run never revokes a token or resets data another in-progress run is using; when another live run is detected, setup fails fast with a clear message; tokens from hard-killed runs are still swept. Document the side-by-side rule in `qa-suite/tests-readme.md`. Deep-dive first and pick the simplest robust liveness mechanism; if there are materially different designs with real trade-offs (e.g. needs a backend change), stop and report options with a recommendation before building.

## Environment
- Ryan's app runs on 8080 (current main build). NEVER run the qa-suite against 8080 or stop/restart it. Boot your own backend from the worktree on the lowest free of 8081-8089 (`lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN`), record its PID, and kill only that PID when done. Postgres (5432) and Redis (6379) are already up and shared.
- Hard-won launch notes live in Ryan's memory dir `/Users/ryanducharme/.claude/projects/-Users-ryanducharme-dev-orci/memory/`: read `reference_run_worktree_app_second_port.md`, `reference_liquibase_utc_guard_blocks_local_boot.md`, `reference_java25_local_jdk.md`, `reference_orci_readiness_signal.md`, `project_maven_stale_classpath.md`, `reference_qa_suite_concurrent_token_sweep.md`, `reference_curl_blocked_use_node_http.md` before booting. If you cannot point the suite at your port without editing that shared file, stop and report.
- Another agent is working a backend ticket at the same time and may also take a port in 8081-8089; re-check `lsof` right before you bind.

## Proof the ticket requires
Start a second run partway through a first against YOUR backend: the first finishes with no 401 and its patients intact; the second fails fast with the message. Then show a token left by a killed run is still swept. Also show the red: the same collision on the unfixed code (or with the guard disabled) producing the 401s. Capture real output.

## Rules
- Scope: only this ticket. Other findings: report as proposed follow-ups; do not fix them, do not create Jira tickets.
- No code comments (repo rule). No Co-Authored-By / generated-with trailers. Commit subject `OR-3086: <imperative summary>` under 72 chars.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run check:tags` clean in qa-suite.
- Jira: confirm assigned to Ryan. No status transitions by you; never Done. In Jira comments never write the parent epic's key or any sibling ticket key; link the PR by full URL.
- This is qa-suite e2e work, which the workon skill treats as a HARD STOP: after your proof runs, do NOT commit/push/open a PR. Leave the changes uncommitted in the worktree and report back; the orchestrator will tell you when to close out.
- Never merge, never run `worktree-done`.

## Terseness (Ryan wants everything human-facing short)
Draft, but do not post yet: PR title; PR body (1-2 sentence summary, at most 4 one-line bullets, `Fixes OR-3086`, nothing else; use `.github/pull_request_template.md`); Jira comment (at most 5 short lines: cause, fix, how proven). Error messages and readme text: shortest precise wording.

## Report back (final message, under 35 lines)
Worktree path/branch; design chosen and why in 2-3 lines; files changed with line counts; exact commands run with real results for the green and red proofs; backend PID/port and whether you stopped it; drafted PR title/body and Jira comment; follow-ups or open questions; anything skipped or unverified, stated plainly.
